title: Private upgrade conductor: Helm/operator-based upgrade tooling + gated migrations
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Goal: Ship a robust, operator-driven upgrade conductor for Redwood Private that executes orchestrated in-place upgrades (control plane + data plane) with explicit rollout gates, preflight checks, and reversible migration steps. The conductor must support air-gapped environments (OCI tar bundles), Helm & operator delivery, LTS channel pins, canary waves, and safe DB/schema+state transitions across versions. This ticket implements the core upgrade controller, migration job runner, and rollout gating primitives used by the Private control-plane and the on-prem operator.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A Kubernetes operator controller (upgrade-conductor) that can: schedule an upgrade across a 3-phase rollout (preflight -> wave rollout -> postflight), apply Helm chart upgrades or operator-managed manifests, and execute named migration jobs in order. 2) Preflight checks: image availability, disk space, kube version compatibility, CRD version compatibility, KMS connectivity (if enabled), and backup snapshot completion. 3) Rollout gating: support canary percentage by node/pool, manual hold with annotated reason, automatic rollback on health-check failure. 4) Migration jobs are idempotent, resumable, and write progress to a migration-status CRD. 5) Air-gap support: controller can load images and artifacts from a bundled OCI tar or local registry and validate checksums. 6) Integrations: emit events to Console (rollout status), and record upgrade operations in audit log. 7) Runbook and one-click rollback tested in staging and documented.
technical_notes: Design summary: Build upgrade-conductor as a clustering-aware K8s controller that orchestrates Helm releases (via helmfile/Helm SDK) or direct manifest application for non-Helm modules. Introduce a new CRD: UpgradePlan {spec: targetVersion, channel(LTS|stable|edge), waves:[{selector, percent}], migrations:[{name, image, command, preChecks, timeout}], rollbackPolicy}. Each migration job runs as a Kubernetes Job in a control-plane namespace and uses a migration-runner binary that performs idempotent steps and checkpoints state to the migration-status CRD. Use leader-election to prevent concurrent plan execution. For air-gapped installs, support bundle unpack: images (OCI tar), helm charts (tgz), and migration artifacts. Use signature verification and checksum validation for all unpacked artifacts. Versioning: semantic-version pinning, LTS channel mapping, and model where control plane enforces compatible runtime schemas. DB migrations: use ordered SQL/etcd migration manifests with explicit 'migrator' container that attempts transactional application where possible and emits safe-guards (dry-run, validate constraints).
security_considerations: All migration binaries must run with least privilege, and any access to secrets (KMS keys, DB creds) must be fetched via the cluster's KMS integration or Secrets store and not baked into images. Signed bundles only; verify signatures against Redwood keyring. Add rate limits and RBAC checks to the UpgradePlan CRD so only authorized roles (enterprise-admin) can create/approve plans. Security review required before GA.
rollout_plan: - Phase 0 (preflight): Run preflight checks, create cluster snapshot (etcd/DB dump) and verify artifact signatures. - Phase 1 (canary): Apply control-plane upgrade on a small pool (10%) and run smoke tests + health checks for 10 minutes. - Phase 2 (waves): Incrementally upgrade remaining pools by configured percentage/wave with automated validation between waves. - Phase 3 (postflight): Run post-upgrade migrations, consistency checks, metrics regression check, and mark plan complete. - Manual hold: operator can annotate UpgradePlan with 'hold' to pause between phases. Auto-rollback: if N consecutive node-level health checks fail, revert Helm release to previous revision and run migration rollback hooks.
rollback_plan: Rollbacks must be migration-aware: if migrations are reversible, run registered reverse steps; otherwise fail fast and alert SRE with explicit recovery runbook. The operator keeps the previous Helm revision; to rollback: 1) Pause plan, 2) run rollback hooks for any reversible migration (migration-runner --rollback), 3) restore DB snapshot for irreversible state, 4) rollback helm release to previous revision using Helm SDK, 5) verify system health and resume. Document the required customer communication timeline for irreversible rollbacks.
risks_and_mitigations: - Risk: Long-running migrations cause cluster disruption. Mitigation: migrate in small batches, implement migration timeouts and accept partial progress checkpointing. - Risk: Air-gapped artifacts corrupted. Mitigation: include checksums and signature verification; require manual approval if verification fails. - Risk: Operator bug causes double-apply. Mitigation: leader-election, migration-status checkpointing, idempotent migration-runner. - Risk: Schema incompatibility with older agent versions. Mitigation: preflight agent version checks and automatic compatible-agent rollout policies.

Wave/canary rollout logic and health-check hooks

Security review and threat model update
Create e2e test harness that simulates failed migration and rollback
